transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-27
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya T. (Redwood AE), Daniel R. (Redwood SE), Sara L. (Arcadia Head of Platform), Owen P. (Security Lead), Luis R. (SRE), Nina W. (IT Ops)

Summary:
High-level kickoff to wire up SSO (SAML), establish SCIM sync for user provisioning, and agree on RBAC/least-privilege model. Discussed SOC 2 evidence, audit logs retention, K M S integration for encryption, and EU data residency concerns. Action items agreed to send metadata, role mapping template, and schedule a SCIM pilot.

Topics discussed:
- SAML configuration (IdP/SP metadata, assertion attributes)
- SCIM provisioning options and delta sync cadence
- RBAC model: role segmentation, least-privilege, ephemeral access patterns
- Compliance: SOC 2 controls, ISO requirements, audit log retention and export
- Encryption: KMS/HSM options, customer-managed keys versus Redwood-managed keys
- Network: VPC peering vs IP allowlist for private deployments

Action items (captured in metadata)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: ok everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off. i'm Maya, account lead for your Redwood work. quick round robin?
[00:12] Sara: hey all, Sara here, Head of Platform at Arcadia. we're trying to get SSO nailed down and a sensible role model before we go prod.
[00:21] Owen: Owen, security. main concerns are encryption at rest with our K M S and log retention for audits.
[00:30] Daniel: hi folks, Daniel, infra SE. i'll be handling the technical runbook and the SCIM pilot.

[00:42] Maya: great, high level plan — SAML first for auth, SCIM to provision groups/roles, then map SCIM groups into Redwood roles. we also want to align on SOC 2 controls, yes?
[00:55] Nina: yeah, from Ops side we need to know the network flows. are you host-only endpoints or do we need a VPC peering?
[01:05] Maya: good question. for hosted customers we use TLS endpoints over the public internet, best practice is IP allowlisting for the SCIM endpoints; for private deployments we can do VPC peering.
[01:18] Owen: which endpoints exactly would need allowlisting? we need to include them in our firewall change request.
[01:24] Daniel: i'll attach the list — but note there are a couple of dynamic egress ranges for autoscaling. we can do a static egress range for the Dedicated/Private route.

[02:00] Sara: on SAML attributes, we should be explicit: we expect nameid, email, and a groups claim. do you require a specific group format?
[02:11] Daniel: we can accept groups as either a claim or a separate attribute. recommended convention is prefix with org- or team-. we'll share a small mapping template.
[02:22] Owen: for SCIM, do you support delta syncs and group membership updates? we cannot afford full re-provisions during business hours.
[02:31] Daniel: yes, SCIM v2 with delta support. typical cadence for pilot is every 5 minutes; we can tune to 15m for lower overhead.

[03:05] Maya: audit logs — we persist admin and auth events for 90 days by default, with export available to your S3; is 90 days sufficient for you?
[03:16] Owen: for SOC 2 we usually keep 12 months, sometimes longer depending on scope. can we push logs to our S3 with server-side encryption using our K M S?
[03:27] Maya: yes, we support log export to customer S3 and you can opt to use customer-managed keys via K M S. there might be an enterprise option for longer retention.

[03:50] Nina: any differences if we go Redwood Dedicated vs hosted? specifically around data residency and auditability.
[03:58] Daniel: Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and you can choose region; private deployments give full VPC control and on-prem options. hosted is multi-tenant with clear SLA but data residency is region-limited.
[04:12] Sara: we are EU-first — all data must remain in eu-central region. can hosted meet that?
[04:19] Maya: yes, we can pin your tenant to eu-central for hosted. if you need on-prem, that's a different contract.

[04:45] Owen: encryption at rest: we need to ensure model caches and any persisted prompt logs are encrypted with our keys. is KV cache included?
[04:55] Daniel: KV cache files on Dedicated can be encrypted; for hosted we encrypt at rest with Redwood-managed keys by default but you can opt into customer-managed K M S for sensitive workloads. we will call out exactly where ephemeral caches live.

[05:20] Sara: example role model: we want three tiers — viewers, editors, and admins. editors can invoke generation endpoints but cannot manage billing or invite new users. admins do invites and can see audit logs. does that map cleanly?
[05:33] Daniel: yes, that's straightforward. we typically recommend more granular runtime roles for production: inference-only, tooling, and admin. we can show sample RBAC policies.

[06:00] Owen: question — is there a way to do just-in-time elevated access for debugging? we have a policy to avoid standing admin sessions.
[06:08] Maya: yes, we support ephemeral access via time-limited role elevation and require MFA on the IdP side. Redwood's console supports audit of the elevation event.

[06:40] Nina: any blockers for JIT? we need SSO to map the role and then a workflow to request elevation?
[06:48] Daniel: two options: map a SCIM group for privileged access and use your IdP's approval flow, or use our built-in request flow that triggers an approval email. both get logged.

[07:12] Sara: on compliance docs — can you share SOC 2 type 2 report redacted and the ISO attestation?
[07:20] Maya: yes we have a secure portal link. i'll share SOC 2 summary and our ISO 27001 certificate. full reports require an NDA in some cases.

[07:45] Owen: do you keep a full audit trail for configuration changes? we need to show who changed role mappings and when.
[07:54] Daniel: yes, config changes are captured and immutable in the audit log; we capture actor id, timestamp, before/after.

[08:20] Sara: ok on SCIM group naming — we'll standardize on arcadia_org_team-<name>. can you accept that?
[08:29] Daniel: yes, that's fine, we'll map arcadia_org_team-data-eng to the 'data-engineer' role.

[09:00] Maya: small note on connectors — some customers use Okta or Auth0 as IdP; we have prebuilt guides for both. any preference?
[09:09] Owen: we use Okta primarily, but have a test Auth0 tenant for one subsidiary.
[09:15] Maya: we'll send both guides and sample SAML metadata.

[09:40] Nina: about SAML assertions — do you require signed assertions, and do you accept SHA-256?
[09:46] Daniel: we do require signed assertions and accept SHA-256, and for cert rotation we support multiple active certs in metadata.

[10:15] Sara: there's also an internal compliance ask — we can't allow service providers to store PII in logs. do you scrub PII from request logs?
[10:25] Daniel: by default we redact user content from logs, but metadata like user-id and email may be retained for audit. we can configure additional redaction on request.

[10:55] Owen: if we want customer-managed keys — how is key rotation handled? can we revoke and rotate without downtime?
[11:04] Maya: in most cases we hand off key management to your K M S; rotating keys is coordinated, and our system does a graceful re-encryption pass that avoids downtime for live data, but ephemeral caches will be flushed and rebuilt.

[11:40] Sara: timeframe — we're planning to run a small pilot in mid-may and go to prod by end of q2. is that realistic?
[11:49] Daniel: mid-may pilot is doable: SAML config + SCIM mapping + RBAC spreadsheet and a small user cohort.

[12:15] Owen: any known issues with matching groups when there are nested groups in Okta?
[12:22] Daniel: nested groups can be flattened in our SCIM sync; we recommend avoiding deep nesting for clarity. we'll document edge cases.

[12:55] Nina: how do you handle deleted users? do you do soft-deletes or immediate deprovision?
[13:03] Daniel: we support both: immediate removal from RBAC and a configurable soft-delete grace period to allow audit and recovery.

[13:30] Sara: audit exports — is there an API or do you push to S3?
[13:36] Maya: both. we can push to your S3 bucket with SSE-KMS, or you can pull via admin API.

[14:00] Owen: what about rate limits for SCIM? large orgs have bursts during onboarding.
[14:07] Daniel: standard SCIM rate limits are documented; we can temporarily increase for onboarding windows.

[14:45] Maya: let's run through the exact attributes we need for SAML and SCIM — i'll share as a single doc.
[14:52] Daniel: required SAML: NameID/email, FirstName, LastName, groups claim. SCIM schema: id, userName, active, groups[]. sample payload will be attached.

[15:20] (Small crosstalk, someone briefly muted/unmuted)

[15:40] Owen: security review aside — do you do periodic pen tests and publish results?
[15:47] Maya: we do internal and third-party penetration tests, we maintain a summary and remediation timeline; we can share the executive summary.

[16:20] Sara: about least-privilege — for us, inference endpoints should be callable only by service accounts, not by product testers. is there service account separation?
[16:29] Daniel: yes, we support service accounts with scoped tokens, and usage can be tied to a specific role. token creation is audited and can be time-limited.

[17:00] Nina: on token rotation — is there a CLI or API to rotate service tokens?
[17:06] Daniel: yes API and Console UI; we recommend short-lived tokens for automation.

[17:40] Owen: any additional compliance options for healthcare customers (PHI)?
[17:47] Maya: we have an enterprise package and private deployments on-prem options that help meet HIPAA-like controls; we'd engage legal for BAAs.

[18:20] Sara: what about retention controls for prompts/explainability data — we need to keep prompts for debugging but redact content for privacy. can we configure retention per project?
[18:32] Daniel: yes retention is configurable per-project and per-route; we can also enable automatic redaction before storage.

[19:00] (Brief pause)

[19:15] Nina: for the SCIM pilot, how many users should we include? what's recommended?
[19:22] Daniel: start with 10-20 users across 3 groups; that gives good coverage for role mapping and edge cases.

[19:50] Owen: about the role mapping spreadsheet — will it include sample policies for rate limits and allowed endpoints?
[19:58] Daniel: yes we'll include columns for permitted endpoints, token scopes, and rate-limit classes.

[20:30] Sara: internal stakeholders: security, infra, and product will sign off. we need a brief runbook and test plan for the pilot.
[20:39] Maya: we'll produce a pilot runbook and checklist.

[21:15] (Background keyboard sounds)

[21:30] Owen: exception handling if a user's group changes mid-run — will RBAC be enforced immediately?
[21:38] Daniel: membership changes are applied at the next sync; we also have webhook notifications for critical changes to enforce near real-time behavior if needed.

[22:05] Sara: ok let's talk about the SAML metadata exchange — how do we accomplish cert rotation safely?
[22:13] Maya: send metadata with both old and new certs included, Redwood will validate and support overlapping validity. we'll guide on best practices.

[22:40] Nina: do you support IdP-initiated login flows in addition to SP-initiated?
[22:47] Daniel: yes both are supported. just confirm ACS URLs in the metadata.

[23:15] Owen: logging detail — is there user-level forensic logs for a given request id?
[23:22] Daniel: yes each request has a trace id; you can query and pull full context for audits.

[23:55] Sara: are there any server-side PII filtering rules out of the box? we want to avoid storing SSNs, credit card numbers in logs.
[24:03] Daniel: default redaction removes common PII patterns but recommend you enable stricter redaction rules for sensitive tenants.

[24:30] Maya: switching gears — timeline recap: Maya shares docs by may 1, Daniel shares role mapping by may 4, Arcadia confirms IdP attributes by may 3, and pilot scheduled week of may 11.

[25:05] (Longer pause, 30s silence as people type)

[25:40] Sara: anything else on legal? we will route SOC 2 review through compliance.
[25:47] Maya: i'll include a link to the portal and the contact at our compliance team.

[26:15] Owen: small nit — you mentioned the KV cache earlier. can you clarify where that lives and how we can control retention?
[26:23] Daniel: KV cache is ephemeral by design; on Dedicated it's on encrypted volumes in your region. retention is short, but we can increase TTLs.

[26:55] Nina: will the SCIM sync create roles automatically or just link groups to existing roles?
[27:02] Daniel: SCIM can create users and groups; role creation is typically done via admin UI or API. for pilot we'll pre-create roles and map groups to them.

[27:30] Sara: what's the rollback plan if provisioning mis-maps privileges?
[27:37] Daniel: we keep a history of mappings and a one-click rollback to the previous mapping; changes are versioned.

[28:00] Owen: question about MFA enforcement — do you rely on IdP policies or can Redwood require MFA?
[28:08] Maya: MFA should be enforced at IdP level; Redwood enforces session timeouts and can require step-up auth for sensitive actions.

[28:40] (Short laughter)

[29:00] Sara: demo request — could you show the mapping UI and audit logs?
[29:06] Daniel: yes let's share screens — (screen share) — ok, opening the console, here's the role mapping page...
[29:30] (Screen share walkthrough, some description: mapping arcadia_org_team-data-eng -> data-engineer, sample audit entry)

[31:00] Daniel: here's a sample audit entry: user id, action=role_map_update, actor=maya@redwood.com, timestamp, old role, new role.

[31:45] Owen: that looks good. is the audit export immediate?
[31:51] Daniel: yes on-demand or scheduled exports daily.

[32:20] Sara: a final question on data residency — if we pin to eu-central, are backups and logs guaranteed to stay in region?
[32:29] Maya: yes for region-pinned tenants backups and logs remain in the selected region. we'll include that in the contract.

[33:00] Nina: for networking — what headers do you expect us to add or strip at the proxy layer?
[33:07] Daniel: we expect X-Forwarded-For and preserve TLS client certs for mutual TLS if enabled. we'll send exact header list.

[33:40] Owen: are you supporting mTLS for ingestion endpoints? we prefer strong mutual auth for some routes.
[33:47] Daniel: mTLS is available for Private deployments and can be added for Dedicated with additional config.

[34:20] Sara: internal ask: can we get a short, non-technical summary for execs covering risk and controls?
[34:27] Maya: yes, we'll prepare an executive summary highlighting SOC 2, ISO, K M S, and SSO flows.

[35:00] (Quick restroom break, 60s)

[36:05] Owen: question — if a user is deprovisioned in IdP, how fast is access revoked?
[36:13] Daniel: default is near-immediate on SCIM removal; with polling every 5 minutes typical. we can enable webhooks for real-time.

[36:45] Sara: any performance impact from enforcing strict RBAC on inference endpoints?
[36:52] Daniel: negligible. auth checks are lightweight; the bigger perf hits are large context lengths and batching.

[37:20] Nina: on the subject of logging, do you correlate logs across services for a single request?
[37:27] Daniel: yes trace ids span the ingestion, inference, and audit subsystems so you can trace requests end-to-end.

[37:55] Owen: how about data residency for ephemeral model artifacts — do those ever leave region for warm pools?
[38:03] Daniel: for region-pinned tenants we keep warm pools within region. cross-region failover is opt-in.

[38:40] Sara: can we schedule a follow-up technical deep dive just for the SRE team next week?
[38:47] Maya: yes — next week works for us, we'll propose times.

[39:20] Nina: any compliance checklist items we should prepare before pilot?
[39:27] Maya: yes, we'll send a checklist: IdP metadata, SCIM test accounts, network allowlist, S3 bucket for logs (if desired), and legal contacts for SOC 2.

[40:00] Owen: last technical question — does Redwood support SCIM PATCH for partial updates?
[40:07] Daniel: yes we support PATCH and bulk operations for large syncs.

[40:40] Daniel: quick note on error handling: provisioning failures are surfaced in the console and via webhook; we also retry with exponential backoff.

[41:10] Sara: good — that should cover most cases.

[41:35] Maya: ok to recap briefly: we will send SAML/SCIM guides and role map, Arcadia will confirm IDP attributes and group naming, run a small SCIM pilot mid-may, and we'll coordinate on SOC 2 docs and K M S options.

[42:00] Owen: thanks. one more ask — can you include sample policies for data retention to feed into our compliance docs?
[42:07] Maya: yes, sample policies included.

[42:40] (Some side discussion about scheduling, calendars)

[43:10] Daniel: tech follow-up items: i'll include sample SCIM payloads, role-permissions table, and network egress list.

[43:40] Sara: who should our legal team contact for the SOC 2 report redaction NDA?
[43:48] Maya: i'll loop in our legal contact in the follow-up email.

[44:15] Nina: any open risks you see from our side based on what we shared?
[44:22] Daniel: none blocking; a couple of operational items (confirm group naming, network allowlist) are required but straightforward.

[44:50] Maya: cool, let's call the meeting there. thanks everyone for the time.

[45:00] (Meeting ends — brief wrap and goodbyes)

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Maya: will send SAML metadata, SOC 2 summary, and exec one-pager by 2026-05-01.
- Daniel: will post RBAC mapping template, SCIM examples, and network egress list by 2026-05-04.
- Arcadia (Owen/Luis): confirm IdP attributes, group naming, and test accounts by 2026-05-03.
- Schedule pilot week of 2026-05-11 and a deeper SRE technical deep dive next week.

References shared during the call:
- Redwood SSO quickstart (link sent in follow-up)

End of transcript.
